HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:  This is a 40-year-old female who underwent 
laparoscopic single-port supracervical hysterectomy today complicated by 
postoperative bleeding for which the patient was returned to the operating room 
for laparoscopy.  The patient subsequently remained intubated and was 
transferred to the intensive care unit.  She received 6 units of blood, 2 units 
of FFP and due to concerns for ongoing bleeding, the patient was returned to 
the operating room by Dr. Ruiz and I was asked to assist in her care.  



The patient was encountered on the operating room table and Dr. Ruiz 
performed midline laparotomy as dictated in his note.  At that time, a large 
amount of hemoperitoneum was encountered and I assisted in enlarging the 
laparotomy incisions superiorly packing off the abdomen and temporarily applied 
manual compression to her aorta due to hemodynamic instability.  There was 
subsequent return of adequate pressures and thorough exploration of the abdomen 
was next performed.  Lap pads were removed sequentially from 4 quadrants and 
upon inspection of the left upper quadrant, there was a large amount of blood 
and clot.  Due to concerns for a prior inadvertent splenic injury, the incision 
was further extended upwards toward the xiphoid and after evacuating blood and 
clot, examination of the spleen revealed this to be intact.  The anterior 
surface of the stomach was inspected and noted to be normal.  A nasogastric 
tube was advanced into the body of the stomach under direct palpation.  
Inspection of the right upper quadrant revealed no evidence of any liver 
injury.  Gallbladder appeared normal.  In the right lower quadrant, there was 
some blood within the right pericolic retroperitoneal tissues adjacent to the 
site where the patient had retroperitoneum opened during lysis of adhesions and 
apparent cauterization of endometriosis.  Careful inspection of this area did 
not reveal any active bleeding. The small bowel was run from the ligament of 
Treitz distally to the ileocecal valve and back again.  There was no evidence 
of injury to the small bowel or the small bowel mesentry.  Inspection of the 
retroperitoneum in the area of the aorta and the bifurcation revealed no 
hematoma or evidence of injury.  The large intestine was examined.  The cecum, 
appendix, ascending colon, transverse colon all appeared normal as did the 
descending colon, sigmoid, and rectum.  Within the omentum, there was clotted 
blood noted. There was some hematoma that was thought to be possibly due to 
small vessel bleeding within the omentum and this was ligated with 3-0 Vicryl.  
Remaining inspection revealed evidence of bleeding within the pelvis. This was 
dealt with as dictated in Dr. Ruiz's note.

 

IMPRESSION:  Hemoperitoneum secondary to postoperative bleeding, status post 
laparoscopic supracervical hysterectomy, as well as consumptive coagulopathy 
versus disseminated intravascular coagulation.

 

PLAN/RECOMMENDATIONS:  The patient will continue to be resuscitated and 
transfused per the rapid transfusion protocol in order to correct her anemia, 
thrombocytopenia, and coagulopathy.  Surgical associates will be available 
should additional surgical needs arise.

After approximately one hour, pushing was resumed. After approximately 1.5 hours of additional pushing, the station had descended to +2 station but would not descend further. Recurrent late and variable decelerations were noted and the patient reported exhaustion.

The posterior and anterior blades were placed gently and without difficulty and articulated appropriately. The sagittal suture was palpated and confirmed to be equidistant from both blades, confirming appropriate placement. The patient pushed through the next three contractions with forceps assistance. A right mediolateral second degree episiotomy was cut. With her next contraction, the patient was again instructed to push with forceps assistance and the  head delivered in LALO. The perineum was examined and the episiotomy was found to have extended to a third degree laceration with partial inclusion of the internal anal sphincter. internal anal sphincter was repaired in continuous fashion with 3-0 Vicryl. The ends of the external anal sphincter were grasped with Allis clamps and were repaired in end-to-end fashion with four interrupted sutures of 2-0 Vicryl. The remainder of the perineal laceration was then repaired in standard fashion using 2-0 Vicryl. The right sulcal laceration was then repaired with 3-0 Vicryl in continuous fashion. A superficial laceration was noted on the posterior vaginal mucosa, approximately 2cm in length proximal to the perineal laceration, and was repaired with a figure of eight. All lacerations were confirmed to be hemostatic. Bleeding was noted from the uterus and a small amount of clot was cleared from the lower uterine segment. Bleeding was monitored and was minimal.
